title: The IR-4 Project Invites Involvement from Minority-Serving Institutions
content: For over 60 years, the Interregional Project Number 4 (IR-4 Project) has provided safe and effective pest management solutions for specialty crop growers through stakeholder-driven research. Building on this legacy, IR-4 is working to engage diverse stakeholders from across the specialty crop community to incorporate more voices into their research programs. From entomology to plant pathology and weed sciences, IR-4’s work expands beyond specialty crops and pest management disciplines to help guide research goals and priorities. IR-4 is a national research program funded by USDA’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture (NIFA), headquartered at North Carolina State University with four regional offices (Michigan State University, University of Florida, University of Maryland Eastern Shore, and University of California–Davis). By facilitating U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) registration of sustainable pest management products and technologies, IR-4 helps growers access tools to protect their crops. Healthy, abundant specialty crop harvests—including fruits, vegetables, nuts, herbs, and horticulture crops—are vital to public wellbeing and to U.S. agriculture.
